confidence_notes: I ran five web searches in total: one for the RBA rate and four for Marmaris prices. Restaurant meals, cappuccino and beer are fairly well supported by aggregated, crowd-sourced indexes (Numbeo, Citycost and similar), which broadly agree: inexpensive meal about $10, cappuccino about $3.5, domestic draft beer about $3. Mid-range dinner for two ranged from about $37 to $43 across sources, so I used a value in between. Cocktail is based on undated or approximate tourist-bar guides (roughly £5-10 or about €7 on Bar Street) and set about 2.2x the beer price. I found no direct glass-of-wine price, so wine_glass is an estimate from the local beer and cocktail relationship and a Numbeo mid-range bottle price of about $10; it is the least certain drink anchor. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge for July peak-season Marmaris, a busy resort town with few formal hostels. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any booking pages or listings. Seafront and Bar Street prices run well above backstreet prices, and Turkish lira inflation makes any snapshot age quickly. Turkey could also be classed as Middle East or Europe; I chose Europe because Marmaris is an Aegean/Mediterranean resort market.
comparable_city_reasoning: Aggregated Marmaris price indexes for food and drink, cross-checked against the general tourist-resort pricing of Turkey's Aegean and Mediterranean coast (Bodrum, Fethiye and Oludeniz are cheaper-to-similar compared with Bodrum's premium). Accommodation reflects July peak-season levels for a mass-market Turkish resort town.
